items.stem: The maximum value of f(x) = 2^(x(1 − x)), 0 ≤ x ≤ 1, is
items.explanation: Because 2 > 1, 2^t increases with t, so f is largest where the exponent t = x(1 − x) is largest. That downward parabola peaks at its midpoint x = 0.5, where t = 0.25. So the maximum is 2^(0.25) = 2^(0.25). Trap: the endpoints x = 0 and x = 1 give t = 0 and f = 1, which is the minimum, not the maximum.

items.stem: Consider f(x) = x³ − 6x² + 9x − 8 and the statements: A. x = 1 is a point of local minimum. B. x = 1 is a point of local maximum. C. x = 3 is a point of local minimum. D. x = 3 is a point of local maximum. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: f′(x) = 3(x − 1)(x − 3), so the critical points are x = 1 and x = 3. f″(x) = 3(2x − 4), giving f″(1) = −6 and f″(3) = 6. A negative second derivative means a local maximum and a positive one a local minimum, so x = 1 is a local maximum and x = 3 a local minimum: B, C only. Trap: the sign of the leading coefficient decides which critical point is the maximum.
